articles.title: Metroid Ravenous Preorders Are Already $10 Off at Amazon and Walmart
articles.summary: Physical copies of Metroid Ravenous for Nintendo Switch 2 are now $10 off at Walmart, following the discounts provided to other recent Nintendo preorders such as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. That brings the game down to $59.88, over $10 off the original MSRP of $69.99.
body: Preorders for Metroid Ravenous went live not long after its standout trailer during the recent Nintendo Direct. There's been plenty of excitement since, and we've even seen preorders for the Metroid Ravenous Special Edition completely sell out in minutes across most retailers since the reveal.
But $10 off the standard edition of the game isn't a bad consolation prize if you were unable to secure a preorder for the special edition.

Yet, what's the deal with the immediate $10 discount at Walmart? Well, it's actually fairly simple. As is Nintendo's custom for this console generation, the MSRP for the game is $59.99 for digital copies and $69.99 for physical copies.

We've seen the same thing with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Star Fox, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Switch Sports Resort, among others. It's a pretty easy way to save $10 if you're planning to buy a physical copy anyway.

articles.title: Apex Legends Art Director Says Street Fighter 6 Pushed Devs to Give Characters the 'Thickest Thighs' They've Ever Had
articles.summary: Apex Legends art director Alisa Rastorgueva revealed that the developers pushed the limits of the game’s character models so far for its collaboration with Street Fighter 6 that its heroes became “thicker” than ever.
body: Street Fighter 6 is coming to Apex Legends with special character skins, a decked-out POI, an ambitious Wildcard Takover, weapon skins, and more on September 22.

To celebrate, a handful of Legends are getting the Street Fighter treatment, transforming them into characters from Capcom’s beloved fighting game franchise: Sparrow is Ryu; Alter is Chun-Li; Mirage is Luke; Caustic is Blanka; Wattson is Cammy; Gibraltar is Akuma; Bangalore is Elena; and Pathfinder is Dhalsim.

Each fighter in this delightful selection of characters boasts a striking silhouette with the muscles to match (they are martial artists, after all) — and that was something that challenged the art team when it came to literally breaking the mold of their Legends to make them look like their Street Fighter counterparts.

In a closed session with the media, Apex Legends art director Alisa Rastorgueva revealed that these Street Fighter skins were so muscular that the Legends now have the thickest thighs they’ve ever made for the game.

articles.title: GTA 6’s Stephen Root Is The Franchise’s Second-Ever Emmy Winning Actor
articles.summary: Actor Stephen Root recently confirmed that he will appear in GTA 6, after people correctly identified him as the voice of the drug-runner Brian Heder. He confirmed this on September 13, and on September 14, Root won his first-ever Emmy award for his incredible performance on the show Widow's Bay.
body: In winning an Emmy, Root becomes just the second-ever Emmy-winning actor to appear in a GTA game. The first? That was James Woods, who voiced Mike Toreno in 2004's GTA: San Andreas.

Woods has won two Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Lead Actor --he won for Promise (1987), and My Name Is Bill W (1989). Woods also won a Daytime Emmy Award for playing Hades in the animated TV spinoff of Disney's Hercules.

Rockstar has not officially announced any casting details for GTA 6, but as mentioned, many people immediately recognized Root as the voice of Heder, and Root later confirmed his involvement in the game. It remains to be seen, however, who voices the game's two leads, Lucia and Jason, or any of the other main cast.

Root won his Primetime Emmy for Supporting Actor in a Comedy Series for Widow's Bay, an eerie, humorous show on Apple TV. He plays the central character, Wyck, alongside Matthew Rhys in the leading role of Tom.
points: Actor Stephen Root recently confirmed that he will appear in GTA 6, after people correctly identified him as the voice of the drug-runner Brian Heder.
He confirmed this on September 13, and on September 14, Root won his first-ever Emmy award for his incredible performance on the show Widow's Bay.

articles.title: Apex Legends VS Street Fighter Brings Chun-Li, Ryu, Akuma, and More to the Outlands
articles.summary: Street Fighter is coming to Apex Legends on September 22, bringing its high-kicking action to the first-person battle royale with special skins, a decked-out POI, a Wildcard Takeover, and more.
body: This collaboration hurricane-kicks its way into the Outlands on Tuesday, September 22 at 10am PT / 1pm ET. We’ve outlined everything you can expect from Apex Legends’ Street Fighter makeover below.

● Sparrow as Ryu: “We’re really thinking about personality, playstyle, silhouette when matching our Apex Legends with their Street Fighter counterparts. Sparrow felt the closest to Ryu's grisly self in Street Fighter 6 specifically, and we really wanted to push the muscle definition for this skin.”
● Alter as Chun-Li: “We wanted to make sure Alter could do Chun-Li justice. We pushed the silhouettes of these models and bodies.”

● Mirage as Luke: “Luke is Street Fighter 6’s breakout character, so we really wanted to feature him. Mirage felt like an obvious match in terms of personality, since they never take themselves seriously.”

articles.title: Harry Potter TV Series Casts Arthur Weasley, Moaning Myrtle and Colin Creevey
articles.summary: HBO's Harry Potter TV series has found its Arthur Weasley, Moaning Myrtle, and Colin Creevey, with Rafe Spall cast as Ron's dad. Spall currently stars in Apple TV series Trying, though has also had roles in Life of Pi, Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom, Men in Black: International, and Black Mirror.
body: Portrayed by Mark Williams in the original Harry Potter movies, Arthur Weasley is the good-natured patriarch of the Weasley family, and a recurring character through the Harry Potter series from the second book onwards.

It is Arthur's love of Muggle objects that ensures Harry and Ron can get to Hogwarts in an enchanted Ford Anglia, and in later stories Arthur's position in the Ministry of Magic allows Harry to hear the inner workings of the wizarding world as Voldemort ascends to power.

Other roles announced today include ghostly schoolgirl Moaning Myrtle and the photography-obsessed Colin Creevey. Both have small roles throughout the series, though first pop up in Chamber of Secrets as victims of a mysterious creature slithering around Hogwarts castle. Here, the pair will be played by newcomers Molly Hewitt-Richards and Jasper Ambrose, respectively.

articles.title: Kingdom Hearts’ Kairi Has Suffered Enough, Will Now Headshot You In Fortnite
articles.summary: For the longest time in the Kingdom Hearts series, Kairi has gotten the short end of the stick, but the franchise's upcoming crossover with Fortnite will finally let Kairi fans choose violence.
body: A new trailer for Fortnite's ongoing Chapter 7 Season 4 shows the trio of Sora, Riku, and Kairi in action. The three sport their Kingdom Hearts 2 appearances, and each wields their own Keyblade. They're seen fighting Heartless (or Heartless-like?) enemies in an area resembling their home world of Destiny Islands, hinting that the ever-evolving Fortnite map will add the locale.

It's all set to the Kingdom Hearts 2 theme "Sanctuary" by Utada Hikaru, which still slaps two decades later. There's no footage of the Destiny Islands trio wielding firearms, but Sora using a shotgun and Kairi blasting opponents with an assault rifle will be a sight to see when the skins drop later this week.

It should be cathartic to a degree to play as Kairi in Fortnite, seeing how she's been treated in her own series. Kairi is often relegated to a damsel-in-distress role, and when Kingdom Hearts 3 ( spoilers ahead for that 2019 game) finally put her in an important position as a Guardian of Light, she... gets kidnapped again and is effectively killed off, leading Sora to literally break the laws of nature to save her.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation’s Director Kept Coming Back To The Witcher 3 For Inspiration
articles.summary: Between the release of Final Fantasy 7 in 1997 and the first chapter in the Remake trilogy in 2020, quite a few games have been released and have gone on to inspire developers.
body: "Final Fantasy 6 was a very impactful title for me when I was playing the games when I was younger, when I was a child. But as a creator, I would say that The Witcher 3 would fill that role of what inspired game creation," Hamaguchi said to GameSpot. "When I started working on the Remake series, I would frequently go back to The Witcher 3 and just marvel at the things that that game excels at. It's a frequent one that I revisit."

More than a decade after its release, The Witcher 3 is still considered one of the greatest open-world games of all time, and it's getting a massive remastered edition on September 29. Next year will also see the launch of an expansion, Songs of the Past, which should help with the long wait for The Witcher 4. Fortunately, Final Fantasy fans won't have to wait too much longer for the final chapter in the remake series to land, as Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will launch for PC and consoles in April 2027.

Square Enix is aiming to make this the biggest game possible, with a "planetary scale" world to jump into. Beyond the main campaign to stop Sephiroth once and for all, there'll also be other activities to take part in, like some classic snowboarding fun.

articles.title: Streaming's Best Spy Thriller Officially Confirmed To Return For Season 8
articles.summary: Slow Horses remains the most consistent show on streaming. While many acclaimed TV series take long, multi-year breaks between seasons, this acclaimed spy series has released at least one batch of episodes annually since 2022.
body: The latest season will be based on the ninth and most recent book in Mick Herron’s Slough House series, Clown Town. The announcement comes shortly after Slow Horses ’ latest Emmy win, with Saul Metzstein taking Best Director for a Drama Series with season 5, episode 6, “Scars.” The show’s sixth season returns Sept. 16, 2026, and runs through Oct. 21, 2026. The upcoming season 7, based on Herron’s Bad Actors, was announced last year.

As for season 8, it “sees Jackson Lamb and Diana Taverner face off in their most explosive confrontation yet,” Apple TV’s summary reads. “When a botched attempt to blackmail the Park puts Taverner on the offensive, it is up to Lamb to unravel one of MI5’s darkest secrets and put an end to it once and for all."

Slow Horses is a darkly humorous espionage drama that follows a dysfunctional team of British intelligence agents who serve in a dumping ground department of MI5 known unaffectionately as Slough House. Oldman stars as Jackson Lamb, the brilliant but cantankerous leader of the spies, who end up in Slough House due to their career-ending mistakes and who frequently find themselves blundering around the smoke and mirrors of the espionage world.

articles.title: 007 First Light’s Switch 2 Edition Delayed Yet Again, Here’s How Long You Have To Wait
articles.summary: Developer IO has confirmed that 007 First Light's Switch 2 edition has been delayed for a second time. It's now scheduled for March 2027. The studio said in a notice that First Light's Switch 2 version was delayed "to ensure we deliver the quality of experience players expect." "This additional…
body: "This additional time will go toward polishing the Nintendo Switch 2 performance of the game," IO said.
First Light's Switch 2 version was playable at Gamescom recently, and IO said it was "thrilled by the positive feedback." The same demo will be at Tokyo Game Show this week in Japan.

First Light's Switch 2 version was originally set to launch alongside the console and PC editions in May, but was later delayed to Summer 2026. Another delay for the Switch 2 edition seemed likely given that Summer officially ends on September 22 and IO had not communicated a release date.

Another reason another delay for the Switch 2 edition is not that surprising is because IO boss Hakan Abrak said back in May that the game needed "a bit more time to get it where we want it to be." At the time, Abrak said the game was now targeting late-Summer, but now it's been delayed to 2027.

articles.title: How to help the Sanzhani in The Blood of Dawnwalker
articles.summary: To help the Sanzhani in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you must find their hidden hideout, become friends with the Tsarina, and locate four Sanzhani in need of assistance. Help the four Sanzhani with their troubles, and you'll receive the most precious reward of all: time.
body: Here's every Sanzhani quest location in The Blood of Dawnwalker and how to use them to send letters to Lunka and regain time segments.

The first Sanzhani quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker is called "Good Home," which starts in the Svartrou Outskirts, north of Svartrau City. You can pick it up as soon as the prologue ends, but you won't see a quest icon until you come close. Every other Sanzhani quest is locked behind this quest, so you can't skip it.

Approach the fairy mushroom ring, follow the trail of rings, and investigate the burrow. Once you've completed the "Good Home" quest, no matter the outcome, the Sanzhani Tsarina will give you the "Letters to Lunka" quest, which contains the "Help the Sanzhani" objective; every time you help a Sanzhani, you'll be allowed to send one letter to Lunka.

Because you've already helped the Sanzhani Tsarina, feel free to speak with her to send your first letter. To help the other Sanzhani, you must complete Sanzhani quests. There are four such quests in total (besides "Good Home" and "Letters to Lunka"), but they aren't marked on your map until you approach their starting point, making it hard to find them.
points: To help the Sanzhani in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you must find their hidden hideout, become friends with the Tsarina, and locate four Sanzhani in need of assistance.

articles.title: 'The Lunar Game' quest walkthrough in The Blood of Dawnwalker
articles.summary: "The Lunar Game" quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker tells Boyar Bakir's story. Having joined forces with Farkas the jester, Coen enters the Lunar Tournament for a chance to meet Bakir alone. Whether he finds allies among the contestants, sabotages the competition, or spares Bakir, is up to you.
body: Here's how to solve the odd riddle in The Blood of Dawnwalker 's "The Lunar Game" quest and find a way to fight Bakir one-versus-one.

"The Lunar Game" is a quest related to boyar Bakir in The Blood of Dawnwalker. To obtain it, you must engage in sabotage missions until Bakir's anger gauge is full. Open the court menu to see your current progress.

When the gauge is full, you'll meet a man named Farkas. He'll suggest that you work together to kill boyar Bakir, kicking off "The Lunar Game" quest. If the anger gauge is full but Farkas hasn't shown up yet, just be patient; he'll find you soon enough.

Beware that the tournament always starts in the afternoon. After Coen and Farkas discuss the plan (step one) and he asks if you're ready, you get the option to skip time until the next afternoon, which may consume many time segments. It's far better to use those time segments on other quests or to upgrade your abilities rather than just skip them.

articles.title: Steam Deck 2 plans aren't affected by ongoing component crisis, Valve maintains, as Steam Frame arrives later and more expensive than expected
articles.summary: Valve is in the news again thanks to the impending launch of its Steam Frame VR headset. The developer recently opened up pre-order registration for the £889 / $1,059 standalone headset following months of wait.
body: In a new IGN interview, Valve was asked whether the ongoing memory and storage crisis has had an effect on Valve's plans for the next Steam Deck. "Not really," said Valve developer Pierre-Loup Griffais.
"We've talked before about how we want to make sure there's a very delineated performance improvement for something like a future Steam Deck, I think we're still looking at it in the same way."

What Griffais is referring to is an idea Valve communicated a few times in the past: for a Steam Deck 2 to exist, it needs to offer a generational leap in performance. In 2023, the developer-publisher said that technology doesn't exist yet. Two years later, Valve said it had a "pretty good idea" of what the next Steam Deck might look like. In April, Valve outright confirmed it's working on a Steam Deck 2 and that the device builds on everything learned from developing the original as well as its hardware launches that followed.

articles.title: The PlayStation Blackout Protest Didn't Move the Needle
articles.summary: It's no secret that many PlayStation owners are unhappy with Sony's exclusive focus on digital media. Some even went as far as organizing a digital boycott. For a week, participants pledged to steer clear of anything digital on their PlayStations, whether that means games, the PS Store, or PS Plus.
body: While Nintendo is boasting about its physical game sales and Xbox is working on its disc-to-digital program, Sony has promised to end disc production, pursued legal positions suggesting digital ownership is limited, and is facing a lawsuit alleging the company tried to establish a digital game monopoly.

Additionally, when responding to the negative fan feedback, Sony figuratively shrugged and underlined that ending physical media will not hinder its business. Some PlayStation users decided to respond by organizing a digital boycott. The movement's motto was "no disc, no buy," and while their intentions were good and their hopes were high, it did not have the result some expected.

Mat Piscatella, who works as a video game industry advisor at Circana, a market research company, recently shared some player engagement stats on Bluesky. One user commented on his post, requesting information on the week of the PlayStation Blackout. "Did you guys notice any change that could be attributed to the PS Blackout?" he asked. To this, Mat responded, "No. There was no significant change at all in player count or engagement in our tracking."
points: It's no secret that many PlayStation owners are unhappy with Sony's exclusive focus on digital media.
Some even went as far as organizing a digital boycott.
For a week, participants pledged to steer clear of anything digital on their PlayStations, whether that means games, the PS Store, or PS Plus.
Additionally, when responding to the negative fan feedback, Sony figuratively shrugged and underlined that ending physical media will not hinder its business.

articles.title: Alien Deathstorm's intense, relentless FPS action was a surprise Gamescom highlight - even if it nearly made my brain explode
articles.summary: Let me paint a picture: it is day three of Gamescom; I have seen dozens of fantastic games, spoken to many enthusiastic developers. I am excited and energised by it all, but also at the point of slightly delirious fatigue (not helped by the Gamescom flu determinedly setting in).
body: Alien Deathstorm, as you might have suspected, is not a game with especially exotic ambitions. It's a sci-fi horror FPS built around dynamism, where emergent encounters impact the ebb and flow of its tense action with each playthrough. But foundationally, it's so singular in focus, so confident in its vision, everything you really need to know about it is right there in the title: it's got aliens (lots of them) and a cataclysmic deathstorm, and together, in just 30 minutes, they felt like they'd make my brain explode.

As my demo begins, a voice rings out across the tannoy. They are Scottish, which pleases me. I'm urged to investigate the outpost's wonky reactor, which turns out to be the first of many systems that, inconveniently for me, have all decided to go spontaneously wrong. And even before we get to the shooty stuff, Alien Deathstorm is a wonderfully moody little number, all stark shadows and flickering industrial lights as the storm rages on: sand eddying through the air, shredded cloth flapping violently in the ceaseless wind, rain torrential, and great chunks of outpost debris skidding across water-slicked walkways and tumbling into the unknown.

articles.title: Ubisoft delays Rayman Legends remake Retold a couple of months "to make sure every detail gets the care it deserves"
articles.summary: Ubisoft has delayed the Rayman Legends remake - Rayman Legends Retold - in order to "make sure every detail gets the care it deserves". The game's release date has moved two months from 1st October to 3rd December.
body: The delay was shared on Rayman social accounts. "While the game has officially gone gold, we have decided to take extra time to make sure every detail gets the care it deserves," a statement read.

The post then signalled the arrival of a new "game overview" trailer on 22nd September, and thanked the audience for its patience - assuming the members of that audience are actually patient and not running around screaming.

Rayman Legends Retold was announced in June and, as mentioned, it's a remake of 2015's Rayman Legends - the superb 2D platformer we awarded 10/10 to in our review, back when we used a 10-point scale. The remake features improved visuals, 4K60 graphics, new collectibles and rewards, and - impressively - a free bundled version of Rayman Origins: Enhanced Edition.
Legends Retold is coming to PC, PS5, Switch 2, and Xbox Series S/X, and we'll have more to tell you about it very soon indeed, wink wink, nudge nudge.
